newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends sharply higher vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends sharply higher vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed higher against the dollar on Tuesday as banks sold the greenback on speculation that devaluation of the local currency may have ended for the time being, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.80 to the dollar after opening at 59.13. On Monday it closed at 59.10.
"The rupee shot up mainly due to a signal by the Central Bank to the market," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank left the dollar-rupee exchange rate unchaged despite overseas gains by the greenback, dealers said. Buying and selling prices were at 58.2170 and 59.3931.
"Speculators holding on to positions came into sell," said a Panasia Bank dealer. "They feel the Central Bank may have achieved its devaluation target at least for the time being."
The rupee had been falling against the dollar for sometime and dealers said it seemed the Central Bank had stopped from arresting the fall.
Dealers said the market would be watching the Central Bank's action on Wednesday.
"It could all turn around tomorrow, if the Central Bank pushes the range up. Tomorrow's action by the Central Bank is crucial," the Standard Chartered dealer said.
Overnight call money closed at 10.25 percent after hovering at around the same level for much of the day.
